analysis.investment_thesis: Small civil construction contractor with lumpy revenue (Rs 1 Cr in 2022 to Rs 90 Cr in 2025 suggests a recent business reorganization or IPO-driven transformation, not organic compounding). At 26x P/E for a 13.6% ROE project-based contractor with collapsing FCF conversion and Rs 60 Cr debt, this fails every Munger quality test.
key_strengths: Debt reduced from Rs 109 Cr (2022) to Rs 60 Cr (2025); equity infusion of ~Rs 86 Cr strengthened balance sheet
Promoter holding at 72.38% — skin in the game
key_risks: Civil construction is a cyclical, low-moat, working-capital-heavy business — no durable competitive advantage
FCF collapsed to Rs 2 Cr in 2025 vs Rs 13 Cr net profit — earnings quality deteriorating (FCF/NI ~15%)
Revenue jump from Rs 1 Cr to Rs 89 Cr in one year signals opaque accounting/restructuring; tiny Rs 267 Cr micro-cap with zero institutional cushion
red_flags: Operating CF crashed from Rs 32 Cr (2024) to Rs 5 Cr (2025) while revenue held — working capital bleed
Rs 86 Cr reserves jump in 2025 suggests IPO/preferential allotment; pricing reflects post-listing euphoria, not fundamentals
Revenue of Rs 1 Cr in 2022 for a company 'incorporated in 2007' is a major discontinuity — business is effectively 3 years old in current form
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Invert first: what kills this investment? A civil construction micro-cap where FY22 revenue was Rs 1 Cr and FY25 is Rs 90 Cr is not a compounding machine — it's a recently restructured/IPO'd entity with no track record I can underwrite. ROCE of 15.5% is barely above cost of capital for a project-based business, and the 2025 FCF of Rs 2 Cr against Rs 13 Cr reported profit tells me earnings are being consumed by working capital — classic contractor disease. The Rs 86 Cr reserves increase in 2025 is almost certainly fresh equity issuance, which deflates the apparent "deleveraging" story.

Munger's filter: do I understand this business's competitive advantage over decades? No — civil contractors compete on L1 tenders, have no pricing power, face cement/steel input volatility, and depend on government/private capex cycles. At 26x earnings for Rs 13 Cr of profit with deteriorating cash conversion and no moat, this is the kind of speculative small-cap I'd put in the "too hard" pile and walk away. Price tells you nothing when the underlying business quality is mediocre. Pass.
